sentences.text: As per informant, the marriage of her younger sister Rashmi with the petitioner was solemnized on 13.04.2022 and initially for a period of one month fifteen days, the couple were living happily.
Thereafter, the petitioner and NC: 2023:KHC:39626 his family members were ill-treating and harassing Rashmi on the ground that she had not brought sufficient dowry from her house.

Subsequently, Rashmi got pregnant and even thereafter accused persons had continued to ill-treat and harass her both physically and mentally and she was not being taken to medical examination when she was pregnant.
Therefore, the complainant and her husband had gone to matrimonial house of Rashmi and requested accused persons to take care of Rashmi.

5. On 10.10.2022, the complainant was allegedly informed that her sister Rashmi was found missing from the house since midnight of 09.10.2022 and on enquiry she was informed by accused persons that missing complaint has been lodged.
Thereafter, on the basis of complaint made by the informant's father a criminal case was registered against accused persons for ill-treating Rashmi in furtherance of their demand for dowry.
Informant suspected that accused persons had committed murder of Rashmi and had disposed of her dead body.
In this background, she had approached the police on 21.11.2022 and submitted information, based on which FIR in Crime No.465/2022 was registered by Channagiri Police NC: 2023:KHC:39626 Station.
The petitioner who was arrayed as accused no.1 in Crime No.465/2022 was arrested on 21.11.2022.

sentences.text: The bail application filed by the petitioner before the jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.487/2023 was rejected on 29.05.2023.
It is under these circumstances, the petitioner is before this court.

7. Learner Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that from midnight of 09.10.2022,
Rashmi was found missing and therefore, the petitioner had lodged a missing complaint which had resulted in registering FIR in Crime No.415/2022 by Channagiri Police Station.

He also submits that subsequently on 27.10.2022 father of Rashmi had lodged a complaint before Davanagere Rural Police Station against accused persons alleging about demand of dowry and also ill- treatment given by accused persons to Rashmi, based on which FIR in Crime No.335/2022 was registered by Davanagere Rural Police Station.
In the said case, all accused persons were NC: 2023:KHC:39626 enlarged on anticipatory bail on 19.11.2022.
Thereafter, on 21.11.2022 sister of Rashmi had approached police informing that she suspected that accused persons had murdered her sister Rashmi and had disposed of her dead body.
On the very same day, the dead body of Rashmi was recovered.
8. The sequence of events raises a doubt with regard to correctness of allegation made in the FIR.
There is no material to show that accused persons were ill-treating deceased Rashmi and only after she was found missing, Crime No.335/2022 was registered by her father.
He submits that the petitioner has no criminal antecedents.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been field.
Accused nos.2 to 4 have been granted bail by the Sessions Court and accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
9. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent - State has seriously opposed the bail application.

He submits that the petitioner has committed a heinous crime of committing the murder of his wife who was pregnant and thereafter buried the dead body in a pit which was already dug by him and kept ready in a forest area.
He submits that whats app messages exchanged by the deceased and informant would go to show that the deceased was being ill-treated and harassed by the petitioner and his family members.
The petitioner has murdered his wife who was 6 months pregnant.
Therefore, considering the nature of allegation against him, he is not entitled for bail.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.
11. The material on record would go to show that the marriage of the petitioner with deceased was solemnized on 13.04.2022.
As per complaint averments, only for a period of about 45 days after marriage, the couple had lived happily.
Thereafter, accused persons started harassing and ill-treating Rashmi on the ground that she had not brought sufficient dowry from her parents house.

sentences.text: The whats app messages exchanged between the informant and the deceased would reflect that the deceased was being ill-treated in her matrimonial house by her husband and in-laws and this was informed by deceased to her elder sister who is first informant in this case.

Undisputedly, the petitioner has filed missing complaint alleging that his wife Rashmi was found missing from midnight of 09.10.2022, based on which FIR in Crime No.415/2022 was registered by Channagiri Police Station which clearly indicates that deceased Rashmi's last presence was in the house of the petitioner herein.

14. Based on the first information of the elder sister of Rashmi, FIR in Crime No.465/2022 was registered and the petitioner was arrested and during interrogation he had confessed to the crime and had stated that he had committed murder of his wife and after committing the murder he had buried her dead body in a pit which he had dug in the forest area.
Based on such confession made by the petitioner, the dead body was recovered from the spot where it was buried by the petitioner and other accused persons.
15. As per charge sheet allegation, the petitioner had strangulated the neck of the deceaed with his hands.
The postmortem report would reflect that the thyroid and hyoid cartilages of Rashmi were broken.
As per charge sheet allegation as a result of force used by the petitioner while strangulating the neck of deceased Rashmi with his hands, the fetus had come out from her private part.

After the petitioner had committed the murder of his wife, the dead body was shifted by the petitioner and other accused persons and was buried in the pit which was kept ready in the forest area by the petitioner.
17. The charge sheet material would go to show that there is sufficient materials to connect the petitioner to the crime.

In addition to the same, the whats app messages exchanged between the deceased and the complainant would go to show that the deceased was being ill-treated in her matrimonial house by the petitioner and her in-laws in furtherance of demand made by them for payment of dowry.
The death has taken place within a period of one year from the date of marriage and therefore there is a presumption against the accused persons.

18. Considering the manner in which the petitioner has committed the murder of his wife who was pregnant and the offences alleged against the accused being exclusively NC: 2023:KHC:39626 punishable with life imprisonment or death, I am of the view that this is not a fit case to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
19. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
